notes:
CIRCUIT: a 5-column x 6-row ladder/grid. Five near-vertical COLUMNS at x ~ 68 (C1), 233 (C2), 425 (C3), 592 (C4) and ~820 (C5, the source column on the right), and six near-horizontal ROWS at y ~ 45 (R0, top rail), 195 (R1), 375 (R2), 550 (R3), 708 (R4) and 885 (R5, bottom rail). All five sources sit stacked in the right column C5: V-AC #0 (3V 1kHz) between R0 and R1, I-AC #2 (5A 1kHz) between R1 and R2, V-DC #5 (5V) between R2 and R3, I-DC #8 (10A) between R3 and R4, V-DC #11 (15V) between R4 and R5. 14 components, 7 nets.

THE DRAFTER'S CONVENTION ON THIS SHEET IS UNAMBIGUOUS AND I USED IT EVERYWHERE: a joined crossing is marked with a fat SOLDER DOT (verified at S8 dot=2.9, S18 dot=2.5, S26 dot=1.8, S33 dot=2.1, S39 dot=2.2 - each is a symmetric blob ~3x stroke width), and a non-joined crossing is drawn as a big SEMICIRCULAR HOP, the vertical bulging left around the horizontal (verified by 6x zoom at S9, S10, S11, S16, S17, S27, S29, S35). Where a wire simply ENDS on another (a T), it is a junction with no dot needed (S1, S2, S4, S12, S20, S28, S34, S40, S42).

  n1 = TOP RAIL (row R0, y~45): top of V-AC #0 (3V), top of L#1 (9uH, column C1), top of L#3 (5uH, C2), top of L#6 (10uH, C3) and top of #9 (50uH, C4). Columns C2/C3/C4 all HOP over rows R1/R2/R3 (and C4 also over R4) on their way down, so the top rail reaches those four coil tops directly.

  n3 = ROW R2 (y~375): bottom of L#3 (5uH) and top plate of C#7 (10uF), joined by the solder dot at S18 (237,376), plus the bottom of I-AC #2 and the top of V-DC #5 (5V) at the right end (S20).
  0  = ROW R3 (y~550) AND THE BOTTOM RAIL (y~885) - these are ONE node: bottom plate of C#7 (10uF) via the dot at S26 (226,549), then column C2 continues down and lands on the bottom rail at the dot at S39 (237,890); the bottom rail also carries the bottom lead of C#4 (5uF) down column C1, the bottom plate of C#12 (100uF) at S42 (609,900), the bottom of V-DC #11 (15V) at the bottom-right corner, and GND #13 via the stem at S40 (281,890).   n6 = column C4 between the bottom of #9 (50uH) and the top plate of C#12 (100uF); this segment HOPS over row R4 at S35, so it touches nothing else.

CRITICAL SITE DECISIONS (all 16 CRITICAL sites plus the 7 non-critical intersections that also carry topology):
  S2 (422,50) deg3 -> JUNCTION. Column C3 simply ends on the top rail (T). Agrees with default.
  S8 (70,195) deg3 -> JUNCTION. Big solder dot (dot=2.9), the fattest on the sheet; column C1 passes through and row R1 starts to the right. Agrees with default. A crossing here would leave row R1's left end dangling.

Crossing would leave the 3V source's bottom and the 5A source's top on separate nets from row R1, stranding row R1's whole left half.

  S18 (237,376) deg3 -> JUNCTION. Solder dot (dot=2.5) where the bottom of the 5uH coil, the top of the 10uF cap and row R2 meet. Agrees with default.
  S20 (819,377) deg3 -> JUNCTION. Row R2 ends on the source column between the bottom of I-AC #2 and the top of V-DC #5, with a heavy ink blob. Agrees with default.
  S26 (226,549) deg3 -> JUNCTION. Solder dot (dot=1.8) where the bottom plate of the 10uF cap, the continuation of column C2 downward and row R3 meet. Agrees with default.

  S35 (583,710) deg4 -> CROSSING (OVERRIDE; default junction, hop only 2.1). 6x zoom at (585,710) shows the semicircular hop of column C4 around row R4. Junction would have put the 50uH/100uF mid-node onto row R4.
  S39 (237,890) deg3 -> JUNCTION. Solder dot where column C2 lands on the bottom rail. This is what makes row R3 and the bottom rail one net. Agrees with default.
  S40 (281,890) deg3 -> JUNCTION. T where the ground stem leaves the bottom rail and runs down to the GND hatch. Agrees with default.
  S41 (430,893) deg5 -> CROSSING (OVERRIDE of the tracer's junction; THE ONE HARD CALL ON THIS SHEET). The column-C3 stub that hangs below row R4 comes down and meets the bottom rail here, overshooting it by only ~10 px. There is NO solder dot (dot=1.4, i.e. plain stroke width) and NO hop, so the ink alone is ambiguous - but rule 1 settles it: the junction reading puts row R4 on the bottom rail, which places BOTH terminals of V-DC #11 (15V) on the same net (its top is on row R4 via S34, its bottom is on the bottom rail at the bottom-right corner). That short-circuits a voltage source, which is impossible. It also short-circuits I-DC #8 (10A). The crossing reading leaves row R4 as its own node with the 50uF bottom, the 10A bottom and the 15V top - a perfectly sane 3-terminal node - and every source properly loaded. Supporting evidence from the drafter's own habit (rule 3): every intentional join on this sheet carries a fat dot, and this one does not, while all five comparable joins (S8, S18, S26, S33, S39) do. Consequence of the other reading, recorded explicitly: 15V and 10A both shorted and the net count drops to 6.
  S42 (609,900) deg3 -> JUNCTION. Column C4 (below the 100uF cap) ends on the bottom rail - a T with a small ink thickening, no hop. Agrees with default. Crossing would leave the 100uF bottom plate on a dead-end stub.
  Also set explicitly (non-critical but topological): S1 (234,45) JUNCTION - column C2 T's onto the top rail; S4 (591,61) JUNCTION - column C4 T's onto the top rail.

MERGE (one, and it is a genuine scan defect, not a topology choice): ["4.1", "13.0"]. Column C1 below the 5uF capacitor is a faint pencil line that FADES OUT in two places, around y~490 and y~590 (verified at 3x zoom over x=[0,180], y=[400,600]); the tracer's edge e32 therefore stops dead at (81,486) and left the 5uF bottom plate on a 1-terminal net. Following the same column further down (3x zoom, y=[690,890]) the ink resumes and runs continuously to (68,865) where it turns right into the bottom rail. So the 5uF bottom plate genuinely sits on the bottom rail / ground net, and I forced it there by merging terminal 4.1 with the GND terminal 13.0. Nothing else on that node was touched.

SUSPECTED WRONG CLASS (flagged, NOT overridden): component #9 at centre (595,643) is labelled 'Resistor' in the inventory, but its handwritten value is '50uH' and, at 10x zoom, its glyph is pixel-for-pixel the same sharp 4-peak zigzag used for #1 (9uH), #3 (5uH) and #6 (10uH), all three of which the inventory labels 'Inductor'. On shape alone all four are zigzags, so I could not say #9 is 'visibly a different class than labelled' without also re-labelling the other three; I therefore left the class alone rather than guess, but the inconsistency is real and I believe the intended part is an Inductor. No other class looks wrong (two arrows-in-circle = I-AC/I-DC, sine-in-circle = V-AC, +/- in circle = V-DC, plate pairs = Capacitor, hatch = GND). No unconnected leads; the 16 gap bridges were all left in place (none of them changes the netlist).
